gen_risks.description: Development of interoperable digital platforms and data sharing creates cybersecurity, data privacy, and unauthorized access risks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Collaborate with CIL and ANSSI to implement strict data privacy protocols, national cybersecurity standards, and permissioned data exchange protocols.
gen_risks.evidence: ensure proper and appropriate application of national data protection and privacy measures... follow security procedures elaborated by ANSSI

gen_risks.description: Inefficiencies or outdated formulas in household targeting could lead to inclusion/exclusion errors in social benefit distribution.
gen_risks.mitigation: Update proxy means test (PMT) targeting formulas using updated 2025 EHCVM survey data and incorporate community-based validation.
gen_risks.evidence: social assistance system is highly fragmented, with more than half of all social assistance beneficiaries not belonging to the bottom 40 percent

gen_risks.description: The implementing ministry lacks an established PIU with financial management staff, accounting software, and experience in financial reporting.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit qualified FM specialists prior to effectiveness, adopt accounting software, establish an FM manual, and implement annual ASCELC grant audits.
gen_risks.evidence: MFS currently does not have a PIU with FM arrangements in place, including the absence of FM staff, procedures manual, accounting software

gen_risks.description: Procurement in conflict-affected regions with limited active vendors restricts competitive bidding, causing price inflation and collusion risks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply World Bank procurement flexibilities for fragile situations, utilize local market assessments, and partner with local NGOs/CBOs where viable.
gen_risks.evidence: procurement in fragile areas with few bidders can restrict competition and possibly increase prices and collusion risks

gen_risks.description: Decline in international humanitarian funding cuts external assistance for displaced populations, increasing pressure on project resources.
gen_risks.mitigation: Strengthen national adaptive social protection systems (PAMPV) and build sustainable institutional capacity to bridge humanitarian and development support.
gen_risks.evidence: Recent cuts in humanitarian funding have reduced support for IDPs

gen_risks.description: Administrative routines and untrained bid committee members threaten to cause significant procurement delays and slow project startup.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit an experienced procurement specialist, train DMP/DCMEF staff and bid committee members, and define strict business standards in the PIM.
gen_risks.evidence: administrative routines may result in procurement delays... bid committee members are not trained in World Bank procurement procedures

gen_risks.description: Delays in adopting operational manuals and signing productive grant agreements could block disbursements under Component 1.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prioritize the preparation and adoption of the Productive Grants Manual and draft standardized grant agreement templates early in implementation.
gen_risks.evidence: no withdrawal shall be made... until and unless the Recipient has: (i) adopted the Productive Grants Manual

gen_risks.description: Heightened risk of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse, and Sexual Harassment (SEA/SH) due to population vulnerability in conflict areas.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement a comprehensive SEA/SH Action Plan, enforce worker codes of conduct, hire dedicated specialists, and integrate anonymous grievance mechanisms.
gen_risks.evidence: SEA/SH risk is Substantial, reflecting the nature of project activities and the vulnerability of the target population

gen_risks.description: Vulnerable categories such as female-headed households, disabled individuals, and IDPs face structural barriers to accessing project benefits.
gen_risks.mitigation: Embed gender-sensitive intake protocols, adapt training schedules, provide mobile childcare facilities, and establish targeted outreach quotas.
gen_risks.evidence: exclusion from the project’s benefits of certain categories of people such as vulnerable groups including women, youth, people with disabilities

gen_risks.description: Fluid political context and potential policy shifts in Burkina Faso could disrupt project execution and institutional governance.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain strong technical engagement across line ministries and formalize steering committee mechanisms anchored in statutory regulations.
gen_risks.evidence: the country’s current fluid political situation

gen_risks.description: Construction of 28 warehouses and center rehabilitations present risks of soil/water pollution, waste generation, and occupational health hazards.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct environmental screening, prepare site-specific ESIAs/ESMPs, enforce strict solid/liquid waste management, and mandate OHS compliance.
gen_risks.evidence: water and soil pollution from solid and liquid waste at construction and rehabilitation sites; occupational health and safety of workers

gen_risks.description: Site selection for storage infrastructure and intake centers may cause involuntary land acquisition or economic displacement.
gen_risks.mitigation: Screen construction sites to prioritize secure public land and prepare site-specific RAPs/LRPs in compliance with ESS 5 where needed.

gen_risks.description: Recurrent severe climate shocks, such as droughts and flash floods, risk destroying beneficiary agricultural assets and livelihoods.
gen_risks.mitigation: Promote climate-resilient economic diversification, provide climate adaptation training, and strategically preposition emergency response goods.
gen_risks.evidence: 5 out of 10 Burkinabe in rural areas affected at least once by droughts or irregular rainfall patterns

gen_risks.description: Fragmented institutional landscape and involvement of multiple ministries risk creating coordination bottlenecks and operational friction.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish an active interministerial Steering Committee and formalize interagency operating protocols led by SP-CNPS and MFS.
gen_risks.evidence: Building adaptive social protection that can respond to the needs of the poor... involves multiple government actors

gen_risks.description: Weak internal contract management capabilities could lead to cost overruns and poor oversight of major infrastructure works.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop formal contract management plans for major packages, leverage experienced external technical consultants, and mandate real-time tracking in STEP.
gen_risks.evidence: insufficient capacity can lead to poor contract management and administration of big contracts

gen_risks.description: Deteriorating security and active conflict in project regions restrict access, endangering staff and preventing direct activity delivery.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement security SOPs, utilize remote monitoring modalities (GEMS, third-party monitoring), and delegate delivery to local CBOs/NGOs or UN agencies.
gen_risks.evidence: high insecurity in some of the areas in which project activities will be conducted

gt_risks.description: Political and governance risk is assessed to be Substantial. The uncertain political and governance context provides a challenge to long-term development policy. Adaptive social protection systems are still nascent and will require continued political commitment.
gt_risks.mitigation: The team, guided by the management, will continue its high-level policy dialogue at central and decentralized levels and ensure continuous advocacy and communication.

gt_risks.description: Macroeconomic risk is assessed to be Substantial. Fiscal space remains constrained by elevated security spending and tighter financing conditions, which increase the risk of reduced budget allocations and delayed counterpart funding for new priorities and reforms, including social protection and the PAMPV. Macroeconomic risks also arise from exogenous factors, including current conflict in the Middle East which can result in a surge in oil prices and put inflationary pressure.
gt_risks.mitigation: Other programs such as the International Monetary Fund program and the World Bank's technical assistance on tax expenditure under the Sustainable Development Finance Policy can help expand fiscal space, partially mitigating these risks.

gt_risks.description: Sector strategy and policies risks are considered to be Substantial. Sectoral strategies and policies remain nascent, and the Government's budget allocation to operationalize the PAMPV remains unclear. Also, sectoral decisions are at times taken abruptly and can heavily affect implementation (for example, the suspension of cash transfers in 2023 led to an increased focus on economic inclusion, and the newly emerged priority of the CONASUR/IDPs led to the revision of the fiche de projet of this project).
gt_risks.mitigation: In parallel with high-level policy dialogue, the project supports strategic communications, adopts an agile approach, and provides technical assistance to promote evidence-based decision-making (with support from SASPP, the Social Protection Response MDTF, and the State and Peacebuilding Fund).

gt_risks.description: Overall fiduciary risks are considered as Substantial, as described in section IV.B and annex 2, based on financial assessment and procurement assessment.
gt_risks.mitigation: The project preparation fund (Grant Facility for Project Preparation) has been used not only to prepare mitigation measures to address these risks but will also elevate the project readiness (for example, effectiveness-linked actions including FM and procurement staffing and initiating the procurement packages for the first 18-months' implementation priorities) to improve the project performance.

gt_risks.description: Other risks related to insecurity are rated as High. The deteriorating and volatile security situation—particularly in regions with high poverty, displacement, and food insecurity that are project intervention areas—will likely be an important risk. The project will also address other risks related to protection of personal data: for Component 2 on social registry and interoperability, activities will be guided by the Information System Security Policy (ISSP) document developed by the ANSSI, to ensure confidentiality of households registered in the RSU.
gt_risks.mitigation: The project activities will be adjusted based on the security situation (see annex 3), and the PIU will be also staffed with a security specialist and a security management plan will be developed. To remain engaged, the project will also rely on remote delivery/monitoring, partnering with local representation (NGOs, UN agencies). The ST-RSU will conduct capacity-building activities, including training sessions and awareness campaigns, to strengthen users' ability to manage and protect households' personal data.
